newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on foreign fund spurt.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on foreign fund spurt.

text.p: Taiwan shares closed higher on Wednesday, though back from early highs, on news that regulators on Tuesday had approved a record one-day influx of US$997 million in foreign investment capital, brokers said.
The index ended up 39.68 points or 0.62 percent at 6,455.44, off a 6,495.42 high. Turnover was an active T$53.51 billion.

"The foreign fund news boosted sentiment, but buying slowed in late trade as many investors think foreign funds usually buy at lows and are not active in pushing prices higher," said Alex Yang of National Securities.
Brokers took note of late buying on construction shares, making the sector Wednesday's second-best gainer, with Der Pao Construction up T$1.2 to T$27.5.
Plastics rose most on rising raw material prices.
Boosted by rising foreign fund approvals, most foreign fund-concept shares rose, with Nan Ya Plastics up T$1.5 to T$55 and Formosa Plastics up T$1.5 to T$63.

Electronics shares rose slightly at Wednesday's open on news that the U.S. semiconductor industry's book-to-bill ratio rose to 0.90 in August from a revised July ratio of 0.86, but closed lower in a wider consolidation, brokers said.
Taiwan Semiconductor fell T$1 to T$53.5 and Macronix slid 60 cents to T$34.1.
Brokers said the Securities and Exchange Commission's approval of a record inflow of foreign funds was significant.

"The SEC's approving more foreign fund entries should have a long-term impact to boost the market," said Tank Hung of Yuanta Securities. "The index will likely break through resistance at 6,500 soon."
Consolidation of recent gains is more likely on Thursday, Yang said, forecasting a 6,420-6,500 range.
